No alarm path exists for that specific failure mode (Persist listener has no outer try/catch on the firstOrCreate). Severity P2.
All listeners are synchronous; no sync↔queued mix race.

top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.title: OrderCanceled cascade: ReleaseStockOnOrderCanceled re-throws → kills ReleaseAvailabilityOnOrderCanceled
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.evidence: app/Listeners/ReleaseStockOnOrderCanceled.php:29 explicitly `throw $e;`. Comment block (iter13 P1 STOCK 2026-05-09) defends the re-throw via 'caller already in try/catch' rationale, but Laravel sync dispatcher (vendor/laravel/.../Events/Dispatcher.php:233-269) halts on listener throw — the next listener `ReleaseAvailabilityOnOrderCanceled` (registered immediately after in EventServiceProvider:167-170) NEVER runs. ReleaseAvailabilityOnOrderCanceled.php has ZERO try/catch of its own, so even if it ran, it'd propagate too.
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.impact: Stock ledger released but availability counters NOT released → divergent ledgers under failure. Idempotent re-execution from the retry queue helps ONLY if the listener is re-fired in isolation, which Laravel does NOT do — the entire cascade is re-fired and ReleaseStock will fail again, never reaching ReleaseAvailability.
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.fix_recommendation: Either (a) move ReleaseStockOnOrderCanceled to LAST position (avoid blocking the availability release) OR (b) replicate the WG-2 envelope pattern (log + dispatch StockDecrementFailedEvent + no re-throw).

top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.title: RefundCreated cascade: ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated + ReleaseAvailabilityOnRefundCreated have ZERO try/catch
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.evidence: app/Listeners/ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated.php is 14 lines, calls app(StockService::class)->releaseForOrder() with no envelope. ReleaseAvailabilityOnRefundCreated.php same. The PRECEDING listener (PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedOnRefundCreated) IS hardened — so the refund broadcast goes out. But if stock release throws, availability release never runs → same divergent-ledger class as Concern 01.
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.impact: Refund persists + broadcasts fine; ledgers diverge on stock-release failure. Asymmetric vs OrderCreated cascade which has WG-2 envelopes on both decrement listeners.
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.fix_recommendation: Wrap both release listeners in WG-2-style try/catch + log + structured fail event. Mirror DecrementStockOnOrderCreated / DecrementItemAvailabilityOnOrder pattern.

top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.title: Outbox-first doctrine violated on 2 events: ItemAvailabilityChanged + StockLevelChanged
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.evidence: EventServiceProvider:191-199 ItemAvailabilityChanged listener order is [BumpSnapshot, InvalidateCache, PersistCatalog, PersistItemAvailability] — outbox persisters are LAST. EventServiceProvider:256-260 StockLevelChanged is [InvalidateCache, PersistCatalog, NotifyStockLow] — cache invalidate is FIRST. Contradicts the doctrine stated in EventServiceProvider:134-143 for OrderCreated ('Persist*ToOutbox MUST run BEFORE side-effect listeners').
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.impact: Mitigated by outer try/catch envelopes on the side-effect listeners — they swallow on failure. BUT: if a swallow body itself fails (Log facade resolution mid-rebind, Cache driver mid-flight crash before the catch frame catches it, or a Throwable that's actually a fatal Error not normally re-throwable), the outbox row is NEVER persisted and the broadcast NEVER goes out. Frontend never learns of the availability/stock change.
top_3_listener_ordering_concerns.fix_recommendation: Reorder both arrays to put Persist*ToOutbox FIRST. The Bump/Invalidate listeners read from the same DB rows the Persist listeners read — no inter-listener data dependency.

additional_observations: Strong defense-in-depth pattern overall: events use DispatchableAfterCommit, most listeners have outer try/catch with structured logging, the 3 critical Order* outbox listeners escalate via OutboxBroadcastSwallowedEvent → Log::channel('fiscal')->critical (pager-grade).

PARITY DRIFT: only 3 of ~11 Persist*ToOutbox listeners (Order Created/StatusChanged/PaymentStatusChanged) wire the OutboxBroadcastSwallowedEvent escalation. CouponChanged / SettingsUpdated / BranchStatusChanged / CatalogChanged / TableChanged / PaidAtCounter / ItemAvailability / ItemExtra / ItemVariation outbox listeners use Log::warning only. If broadcaster is down + outbox-retry cron is down, these swallow silently.

BRAIN claim '11 listeners ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit (subagent fan-out missing)' is STALE — verified TODAY: 0 listeners implement that interface; codebase uses event-side DispatchableAfterCommit trait instead. Recommend updating BRAIN to reflect actual design choice.

ZReportClosed event mentioned in this task's spec does NOT exist in this codebase — no fiscal-close domain event is dispatched. If audit consumers need a hook, this is a separate gap (out of scope for I.4).
All 16 events audited use DispatchableAfterCommit trait correctly. No synchronous dispatch inside an open DB::transaction was found (good — broadcaster cannot observe pre-rollback state).
DispatchableAfterCommit::dispatchNow() exists as a test-friendly bypass — verified by tests/Feature/Outbox tests calling dispatchNow when forcing immediate behavior.
verdict_rationale: 1 RED ordering bug (Concern 01: OrderCanceled re-throw kills availability release), 2 AMBER concerns (Concern 02 + 03), well-isolated overall but with documented asymmetric hardening and 2 doctrine breaches. Production-safe under normal conditions; degrades to ledger drift or silent broadcast loss under specific failure modes. Recommendation: fix Concern 01 immediately (one-line change), schedule Concern 02 + 03 for next quick-win wave.
